model_annotation: Figure 10 illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, with error bars indicating the standard deviation. The horizontal axis displays language family categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-Other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, listed alphabetically. The vertical axis is labeled “effect” and represents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30, with tick marks at 5-unit intervals.  Bars are presented in a single series, each corresponding to a language family and colored in shades of teal and purple. The IE-Baltic bar is the shortest, measuring approximately 2, while the Uralic bar is the tallest, reaching approximately 26.  The IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Slavic, and Semitic bars all have similar heights around 14-16 units. The IE-Romance bar measures approximately 20 units, and the IE-Other bar around 12 units. The bar for the Isolate language family is approximately 8 units. Each bar is accompanied by an error bar extending above and below its height, indicating the standard deviation.
